notes: Evrima RCON is NOT Source RCON. The client opens a raw TCP socket, sends 0x01 + password + 0x00 (the server answers "Password Accepted"), then sends 0x02 + one opcode byte + the arguments joined by commas + 0x00. That framing is stated identically and independently by three implementations: the PHP opcode map (RCON_AUTH 0x01, RCON_EXECCOMMAND 0x02, RCON_RESPONSE_VALUE 0x03), theislercon's messages.go/client.go (Auth 0x01, ExecCommand 0x02, success string "Password Accepted"), and isle-evrima-rcon's protocol.ts (AUTH_PREFIX 0x01, COMMAND_PREFIX 0x02, TERMINATOR 0x00, AUTH_SUCCESS "Password Accepted"). The words recorded in commands are the names community RCON clients type for those opcodes - announce 0x10, serverdetails 0x12, ban 0x20, kick 0x30, playerlist 0x40, save 0x50 - and are what a person types in an Evrima RCON terminal; the server matches on the opcode byte, not the word, so other clients expose different aliases for the same opcodes (smultar/evrima.rcon and isle-evrima-rcon use "players" for 0x40 and "srv:details" for 0x12). kick and ban take the player and the reason separated by a comma - aerond7's command table gives both explicitly as player,reason - and accept an EOS ID, a Steam ID or a player name. No published opcode map contains an unban opcode and no source documents a ban-file path, so unban and banList are omitted; note also that theislercon defines BanPlayer 0x20 but ships no ban method, so ban rests on the PHP, C# and TypeScript clients. Evrima has no hardcoded RCON port: RconPort must be set in Game.ini under [/Script/TheIsle.TIGameSession] alongside bRconEnabled and RconPassword; 8888 is the common self-hosted default used by the community clients and guides, while the developers' own example config shown in the evrima-rcon repo uses RconPort=5555, so the port must never be assumed. Sources disagree on the playerlist response layout: theislercon strips a leading "PlayerList" tag and then splits the ENTIRE payload on commas, walking it in strides of three and taking field 0 as the ID and field 1 as the name while discarding field 2 - it is not line-oriented and never reads an EOS ID - whereas isle-evrima-rcon splits on newlines and reads three column lines holding all Steam IDs, then all names, then all EOS IDs. The recorded playerParse assumes one "id,name,eosid," record per line; a stride-of-three comma split accepts that shape, but no source states it outright, and the PlayerListEnd entry in skipLinePattern is defensive and unattested (PlayerData/PlayerDataEnd are real markers, but they wrap the getplayerdata response, not playerlist). playerParse is the one field that must be re-checked against a live server before verifiedAt is set.
